quotes.speaker: PJ Tucker
quotes.summary_phrase: PJ Tucker on the business logic of LeBron James joining the 76ers
quotes.excerpt: This is why it's wise, too, though. I think it makes a lot of sense.
quotes.quote: This is why it's wise, too, though. I think it makes a lot of sense. Obviously, Josh Harris, I'm a big private equity guy. David Adelman, I think he took over for Michael Rubin. Big real estate guy. Obviously, Michael Rubin still had that connection there from being a previous owner. And I'm sure I'm missing some more guys. Bob Myers, like a lot of behind the scenes.

quotes.speaker: PJ Tucker
quotes.summary_phrase: PJ Tucker on the intensity of 76ers fans
quotes.excerpt: Philly fans, listen, I don't know if y'all seen this. It's the best and the worst.
quotes.quote: Philly fans, listen, I don't know if y'all seen this. It's the best and the worst. They're the best and the worst. I'm telling you right now, Philly fans are my favorite. They really, really do care. But then, as soon as anything goes wrong, you ain't never been booed in the middle of the first quarter. Listen, they do not care. They're going to say it. So, that's going to be interesting to see.

quotes.speaker: PJ Tucker
quotes.summary_phrase: PJ Tucker on the sacrifice required to win an NBA championship
quotes.excerpt: When you get on teams that's actually focused from day one on winning a championship.
quotes.quote: When you get on teams that's actually focused from day one on winning a championship and you know you got the pieces, you got to have guys sacrifice. And that year, Chris Paul, being one of the best point guards that ever played the game, took the step back. And when he did, he started running the second unit. Our second unit started going crazy. We were unstoppable. We went on like a 20-18 game streak throughout the year, won 69 games. It was like we really transformed because of the sacrifice.

quotes.speaker: PJ Tucker
quotes.summary_phrase: PJ Tucker on playing through injury during the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: I had four root canals before Game 6. That's the longest four and a half hour flight.
quotes.quote: I had four root canals before Game 6. That's the longest four and a half hour flight of my life. I'm sweating, going through it. We get to Houston, I get the joint done the next morning, and we had a game the next day. Four root canals at once. I knock them all out at once during the game, right before Game 6.

quotes.speaker: PJ Tucker
quotes.summary_phrase: PJ Tucker on the nature of leadership in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: Leadership is natural. You bring somebody in to assume that role, but they might not fit.
quotes.quote: Leadership is natural. You bring somebody in to assume that role, but they might not fit in that leadership role that you think they're going to fit in, or it might not work out. It's got to be a clash of personalities and games. It's just a way of banding the brothers and getting that together, but it's a natural progression.

quotes.speaker: PJ Tucker
quotes.summary_phrase: PJ Tucker on the changing landscape of youth basketball development
quotes.excerpt: It is a new era of how things are done. My era guys, I grew up playing basketball.
quotes.quote: It is a new era of how things are done. My era guys, I grew up playing basketball in the streets, in the projects with older guys. That is how I feel I got tough, that is how I got good, that is how I was able to do anything on the court. When you played 21 back in the day with older guys, you could not get the ball, you had to get a board. How you learn how to rebound? How I learned how to, when somebody shoot the ball, know if it is going to be short or long or where it is going. That is how you learn by playing basketball.

quotes.speaker: PJ Tucker
quotes.summary_phrase: PJ Tucker critiques modern youth reliance on YouTube for skill development
quotes.excerpt: I watch my son sit in the house and watch YouTube clips of other people doing stuff.
quotes.quote: I watch my son sit in the house and watch YouTube clips of other people doing stuff and I am like, bro, you have a whole court outside. I used to walk 30, 40 minutes just to shoot and hoop every day, getting out of the house, never been in the house. Now, to get them out and to give them the hoop, you have to pay this money, get these personal trainers. I have seen one the other day, kids dribbling and doing these tennis balls and he is picking up, he has a chair in his hand, he is dribbling and holding the defender off with the chair. I am like, bro, what is this? That is not teaching him nothing, it is teaching him how to do exactly what he is doing right now. That is not teaching him to get better at playing basketball.

quotes.speaker: PJ Tucker
quotes.summary_phrase: PJ Tucker on the value of professional trainers for elite players
quotes.excerpt: You have these Phil Handys, the dudes that are really like that, that really train Kyrie.
quotes.quote: You have these Phil Handys, the dudes that are really like that, that really train Kyrie and do stuff for pros and guys that are already on that level. Even kids, I watched him do the stuff with the kids with him and Kyrie, that is dope. That is real training of getting guys better every day, teaching them how to work. If you have seen that at the top 100, I think that was dope. That is what it is about. But you see some of the stuff on Instagram, it burns me out.

quotes.speaker: PJ Tucker
quotes.summary_phrase: PJ Tucker on the challenge of keeping his son focused on basketball fundamentals
quotes.excerpt: Having a 14-year-old son, it is so hard to try to dissociate him in his mind to that.
quotes.quote: Having a 14-year-old son, it is so hard to try to dissociate him in his mind to that, to be locked in and like really getting better every day and playing basketball. That is how you get better by playing. That is how you get better by playing.

quotes.summary_phrase: Unidentified host agrees with PJ Tucker on the necessity of playing pickup basketball
quotes.excerpt: Just being out there at the park, just playing, like even the basketball would flat, still be hooping.
quotes.quote: I agree with you, bro. I ain't going to hold you. I agree with you too. I mean, just being out there at the park, just playing, like even the basketball would flat, still be hooping. A lot of these trainers got mad followers or like they work out with like a famous athlete or their kid and think they like an actual trainer. Like no, it is already actually in the DNA. They are kind of already nice for the most part and I just feel like outside builds character.

quotes.speaker: PJ Tucker
quotes.summary_phrase: PJ Tucker on the importance of playing solo to develop basketball imagination
quotes.excerpt: I used to play a different person every day. By myself, playing full court one-on-one Jordan.
quotes.quote: I used to play a different person every day. By myself, playing full court one-on-one Jordan. What is up? Like I am really talking to myself on the court, ain't nobody near me. That was my imagination, my dream to be where I want to be and that was like the driver force to like really want to work through it, bro.

quotes.speaker: Unidentified Host
quotes.summary_phrase: Unidentified host on the benefits of solo practice for basketball development
quotes.excerpt: I feel like that is when you get better as a basketball player when you just on the court.
quotes.quote: I feel like that is when you get better as a basketball player when you just on the court by yourself and you working on every situation. Someone cutting you off, you trying to work on the game winning shot or you just tired, like every little imagination in your head you playing through. That is when you really get better, I would say for real.

quotes.speaker: Unidentified Host
quotes.summary_phrase: Unidentified host critiques the scheduling of international NBA games
quotes.excerpt: I am going to rent on teams playing overseas. Like overseas traveling when we go to Australia.
quotes.quote: I am going to rent on teams playing overseas. Like overseas traveling when we go to Australia, we go to London, we go to Brazil, all that type of stuff. It is just BS. If you are going to go, go over there for the whole week. Let us stay inside the city or close to the city, not an hour and a half outside of the city. Most people ain't going to never go to London, but we going to London playing on Sunday. You getting there on Saturday or you getting there on Friday. The shit pointless. And then you leaving right after the game. It throw all the whole routine.

quotes.speaker: Unidentified Host
quotes.summary_phrase: Unidentified host argues for better planning of international NBA games
quotes.excerpt: It is up to the coaches and you know the the head people to say, hey, we are going.
quotes.quote: It is up to the coaches and you know the the head people to say, hey, we are going over there this certain time. So I think it is just BS from that. I do love the standpoint, if you are going to do it, especially from like an Australia standpoint, a Brazil standpoint, do it the first week of the season because it make it make a little bit sense. Then you you ain't really throwing off on the on the routine as much. Then you got the whole rest of the season.

quotes.speaker: PJ Tucker
quotes.summary_phrase: PJ Tucker suggests international games should count toward the regular season
quotes.excerpt: I don't think it is fair that those games count. Like them, they should be preseason games.
quotes.quote: I don't think it is fair that those games count. Like them, they should be preseason games. I think like NBA, like we kind of figured it out, like we kind of figured it out like getting there early, getting there to enjoy ourselves, be there a long time. Like NBA, like we did Mexico City, we did Tokyo, that was crazy. Tokyo for like a week, just got the culture.
